avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, controlling emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public property, and pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs add their own resources: money from park funds, equipment rental, blue-collar crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees distributed across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the chalet at parc Pratt and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives and clean streets, sidewalks and bike paths. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the sidewalk cleaning contract for four private snow removal sectors is awarded to Les Équipements Benco Canada ltée for $271,979.11, taxes included [CA26 27 0034].

etapes.titre: Maintenance and snow removal of public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to remove snow, spread abrasives and maintain downtown public squares, including Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord pays an extra $106,150.97 for renting an additional grader [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard draws $200,000 from its surpluses to pay staff and buy salt and sand [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offers city council to provide its own staff for its snow disposal site.

The City is extending turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro by twelve months, along with towing contracts in four boroughs and equipment rentals with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Boroughs are doing the same for their own machine rentals.

aSurveiller.texte: The extended towing contracts for Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension start on November 15, 2026.
The eight turnkey snow removal contracts awarded in August cover four winter seasons and end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is financing and building the disinfection unit for the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, and is awarding several contracts for the maintenance and upgrading of this plant. It is also having water and sewer pipes rehabilitated or rebuilt in numerous boroughs, with replacement of lead service connections, on both the public and private sides. Loan by-laws govern the financing of this work.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections taken on by boroughs
etapes.texte: Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest and Ahuntsic-Cartierville are offering city council to carry out, themselves, the replacement of lead service connections located on private property, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the owners.

etapes.titre: New loans and addition to an ongoing contract
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It adds $12,144,522.14 in contingencies to Pomerleau's contract for the rue de la Cathédrale pipe, toward the McTavish reservoir, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption expected on October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
The ozone plant is expected to go into service in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must end in the last quarter of 2028.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 starting the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, about six weeks each.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
Completion of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at Frédéric-Back park: a greenhouse complex in the park's southwest sector, the upgrade of electrical installations at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, and routine park maintenance. It has also requested funding from Québec for a trail crossing the park from east to west, and launched the redevelopment of rue De Louvain along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Request for funding for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow [CG26 0121].

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse project
etapes.texte: The agglomeration approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood's community greenhouse, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry out the project, and city council accepts.

etapes.titre: Site electrical work and park maintenance
etapes.texte: The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, for $1,091,693.37 including taxes: a new 25 kV supply, transformer, backup generator and automated system to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223]. It also awards Groupe Nicky and Les Entreprises Roseneige the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park, from May 1, 2026, to October 31, 2028 [CG26 0224].

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between Frédéric-Back park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings, in three phases from 2026 to 2028.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator, from June 20 to October 15, 2026, for an additional expense of $296,349.21 including taxes. The compost is used as a soil amendment, notably for the landscaping of Frédéric-Back park [CG26 0320].

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouses is to be completed in December 2026, with commissioning announced for winter 2027.
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway surface, bike path, plantings).
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City added $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones requiring hand cleaning, a greater quantity of mortar, and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase.

The City authorized the submission of an application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application requires no financial commitment; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan and bringing its light fixtures up to standard.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as protected areas
etapes.texte: The City listed the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans providing for ecological management. It also took note of the 2025 area summary.

The City awarded Gendron Gestion Civil inc. a contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45, taxes included. The culvert had been damaged by heavy rains in August 2024.

aSurveiller.texte: The Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan must be submitted in February 2027, DarkSky International's response is expected in April 2027, and full compliance for the site is set for April 2032.
The snow removal contract covers two winters, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
The janitorial contract for the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with an option to extend to October 31, 2031.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is putting in place a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the viaduc Van Horne.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects related to inclusion, cohabitation in public spaces and awareness-raising. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and the Bain St-Denis layout
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and layout work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a statement of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampments area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the litigation over the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampments area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, transitional developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking its agents' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for suggestions held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental soil management. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, then the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 housing units per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for growing sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

Work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street-naming file indicates that site development is planned for around 2032 and that four other public places still need to be named.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water main for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It got more time from the Québec government to sell a first piece of land, guaranteed a loan for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for streets, sewers and the water main in the sector. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not involve any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a $2,000,000 City guarantee in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the organization GALOPH that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water main, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and leisure centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public facilities and equipment in the sector, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first piece of land must be completed by no later than October 31, 2027.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Design and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks designed and renovated in several boroughs: construction contracts, soil studies, decontamination funding, and additional funds for projects already underway. It is also active in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, with work on the chemin de Senneville, snow removal and maintenance contracts, and efforts to protect natural environments and the night sky.

etapes.texte: Borough councils are awarding contracts to redo parks: the Lucie-Bruneau dog park in Anjou, Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun, Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie, Denise-Morelle and Baldwin in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. The work includes play areas, water play features, paths, furniture and plantings.

The City and the boroughs are adjusting contracts already awarded: monitoring of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, contingencies for parc Villeray, budget transfers for parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet, additional fees for parc Denise-Morelle. The City is also paying $168,472.14, net of taxes, to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension for environmental remediation of parc George-Vernot [CM26 0887].

etapes.titre: Land transferred to parks and school agreement
etapes.texte: A section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², is being transferred from public street land to public park land to be added to parc Campbell Ouest [CM26 0704]. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same change for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway in parc Le Prévost. Outremont is ratifying an agreement with the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys and paying $150,000 for the parc-école Saint-Germain.

aSurveiller.texte: Executive committee on October 7, 2026 and city council on October 19, 2026 on the change of status of the laneway strip in parc Le Prévost.
Work on parc Denise-Morelle is to begin in early August 2026 and end in November 2026.
For the Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky response expected in April 2027, site compliance in April 2032.
For the public art at parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner selected in October 2026, contract in December 2026, artwork installation in 2028.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027; work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc continuing until June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares. They adopt funding rules, pay out money to business development corporations, then issue the ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate sales, noise and occupation of the roadway. At the end of the season, reopening schedules are adjusted and two files concern the status and name of public squares.

etapes.titre: Settlement of a dispute over a public square
etapes.texte: The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough settles out of court, for $41,686.46, a lawsuit related to the development work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer. The settlement is concluded without admission of liability.

etapes.titre: Rules and money for the 2026 season
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law setting the conditions for grants to its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, with applications to be filed no later than February 16, 2026. The executive committee then authorizes transfers of $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries.

The boroughs pay out sums to business development corporations and their projects: $102,045 for rue Villeray, $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe. Outremont allocates $105,000, net of taxes, to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards a contract for $287,724.94, taxes included, for on-demand transportation of persons with reduced mobility and seniors on avenue du Mont-Royal, and bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve temporarily removes 113 paid parking spaces, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on a closed street on avenue de Monkland, and the City pays $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street.

etapes.titre: Status, name and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes a 899 square-metre plot of land, at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, from the status of street (public square) to that of local park, and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite." Le Plateau-Mont-Royal divides avenue du Mont-Royal into three sections with separate reopening dates.

aSurveiller.texte: Reopening of avenue du Mont-Royal: between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Full reopening of avenue Bernard to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
The pedestrian streets and public squares of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (avenue Royal, avenue Madison, Placette CDN) remain closed to cars until October 31, 2026.
Boroughs' accountability reporting in November 2026 and return of unspent sums in December 2026.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period up to December 31, 2027; the contribution for avenue Lacombe runs until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and building footprint ratio in the area bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the allowed heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing a lack of staff, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work in the declared heritage site of the Mont-Royal subject to approval.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027, as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027, to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The City adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team on enforcement of the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys patrol motorcycles, extends the housekeeping contract for headquarters by one year, and awards a contract to replace the oil heating system at the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second loan of a police officer to the RCMP, starting March 30, 2026, with an additional budget of $136,260 for 2026.

etapes.titre: Meals for detainees and call-handling software
etapes.texte: The City awards a company the preparation and delivery of meals for persons held in custody by the SPVM, for three years. It also extends by twelve months the maintenance of the patrol dispatch and emergency call-handling software system, and accepts an $8,000 federal grant for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

etapes.titre: Motions of support after the shooting
etapes.texte: Following the shooting on June 22, 2026 in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, borough councils adopt motions of support for the SPVM. They offer condolences to the families and reaffirm their commitment to the police service.

aSurveiller.texte: Secondment agreement for police officers to the RCMP's Synthetic Drugs Integrated Enforcement Team, starting October 12, 2026, for three years.
"Fèves au lard" (baked beans) day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026, for which the Anjou borough buys tickets.
Start of the lease for the metro unit of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, on February 1, 2027.
Delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer by March 1, 2027 at the latest.
Completion of the heating system replacement work at the cavalry building, expected September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

etapes.texte: The City sells a 364.3-square-metre piece of land for $495,150 to expand the entrance pavilion of the Place-Saint-Henri station, land in Verdun for $257,425 to rebuild and expand the Rielle ventilation station, and commits to selling a piece of land of about 202.8 square metres on rue Jean-Brillant for $115,000 to build a rectifier station there. These amounts are shown before applicable taxes.

Elected officials approve several STM loan by-laws and the corresponding amendments to the 2026-2035 capital works program. They concern reserved lanes and priority traffic lights for buses, the rehabilitation of métro and surface infrastructure, cybersecurity, extending the service life of the MR-73 train cars and the analysis of their replacement.

The City buys advertising space in the STM network and at Astral for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50, taxes included, and grants $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships. The executive committee accepts on loan the archaeological collection from the REM excavations; councils adopt motions on the preservation of the blue line's tunnel boring machine and on a structuring public transit project in the east.

aSurveiller.texte: The Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lease begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer vacation period, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; work is planned until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is planned for 2031; the City's work there is integrated in 2028-2029.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths, and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-serve bike system.

etapes.texte: Outremont approved a $100,000 expense, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives used notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awarded a $153,395.05 contract, taxes included, for the rental of a mini sweeper with operator that cleans, in the spring, paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

etapes.titre: BIXI bikes and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for mechanical bikes, electric-assist bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI. It also added $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract of Bruneau Électrique inc. for lights, civil and electrical works, and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

City council approved an agreement of $125,167.62, taxes included, to pay Hydro-Québec the rents from 2014 to 2025 for land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approved a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a plot of about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, at a total rent of $46,896, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Resurfacing of the REV Lajeunesse and avenue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offered to take charge of the resurfacing of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepted this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike lane works. Outremont gave a notice of motion to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: The UCI Road World Championships are being held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; roadway works are planned along the route in Ville-Marie.
Complete financial assistance applications for the rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier projects must be submitted by October 9, 2026 at the latest.
